thesis.title: Leveraging NFV heterogeneity at the network edge
thesis.supervisors: Professor Dimitrios Pezaros and Dr Yehia Elkhatib
thesis.summary: Network functions such as firewalls, load balancers and intrusion detection now run on very different platforms: virtual machines, containers, programmable switches and SmartNICs. The thesis asks how to place chains of these functions across that mix of hosts at the network edge so that latency stays low.
contributions: A taxonomy of heterogeneous frameworks for deploying virtual network functions.
Testbed measurements of what heterogeneous execution actually gains.
An integer linear programming model for hybrid placement across programmable data-plane devices and user-space hosts, minimising end-to-end latency.
HYPHA, a heuristic that finds near-optimal hybrid placements quickly.
A dynamic placement scheduler based on optimal stopping theory that reduces latency violations and migrations.
